Meta's numbers have come through Singular, our MMP, since — on iOS and — on Android. For the same App Store money, Singular credits Meta — (iOS) and — (Android) of what Meta's own attribution did. That is the whole "March break": a smaller ruler, not a weaker business. Every relative finding holds on the new ruler, so the bar moves with it, and absolute Meta ROAS is never compared across the switch.

1 · What the switch moved, and what it didn't

Each metric against its own Dec – mid-Feb average (1.00), by OS

Dotted lines: the switch week of each OS. Numbers credited through the MMP (ROAS, purchases, installs, click → install) stepped down in the switch week. CPM didn't. iOS click-through also jumped in the switch week while click → install halved: the iOS click path changed with the switch (link, landing page or how clicks are counted), so iOS CTR and click → install are not comparable across it either. Hook rate also fell, starting the week before the switch; Meta counts it itself, so that is the creative mix, not the ruler.

3 · Decisions made on the new ruler

Adset by adset, budget moves kept following relative results (— before, — on Singular): the buyer's read of which adsets beat their OS survived the switch. The damage was at account level. Spend fell to about $120k a week in May and June while account Meta ROAS read 0.37–0.40 (red on the old bar, green on the new one), and App Store proceeds fell with it. — adsets were switched off while at or above their OS average.

Where the ROAS went

ROAS = installs per 1,000 impressions (IPM) × install → purchase × revenue per purchase ÷ CPM. Base: —. Now: —.

ROAS moved from — to —. IPM, the install-rate signal you use for demand, changed —; CPM changed —, revenue per purchase — and install → purchase —.

StepBaseNowChangeROAS points it explains

Both windows are on Singular, so the steps compare like with like. "Points it explains" splits the ROAS change across the four steps (log shares); CTR and click → install are the two parts of IPM.

The steps, week by week

Account totals. Dashed line: the base-period value.

Each adset's #1 concept takes — of its spend in a typical week and stays on top for a median of — weeks. The adset's ROAS holds for two weeks of a reign, then slides. Whether a new concept will take over is decided in its first week, by the spend Meta gives it, not by hook rate or CTR.
